_meta.indication: Tasigna is a kinase inhibitor indicated for the treatment of chronic phase and accelerated phase Philadelphia chromosome positive CML in adult patients resistant or intolerant to prior therapy that included imatinib.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study 2101, a phase 2 multicenter study of nilotinib in imatinib-resistant or -intolerant CML
pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: A single open-label multicenter study with separate cohorts for chronic phase and accelerated phase CML.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with imatinib-resistant or -intolerant Philadelphia chromosome positive CML in chronic phase (CML-CP) and accelerated phase (CML-AP); 73% were imatinib resistant and 27% imatinib-intolerant.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary efficacy endpoint was unconfirmed major cytogenetic response (MCyR) in CML-CP and confirmed hematologic response (HR) in CML-AP.
pivotal_trials.n: 438 patients treated (CML-CP=318; CML-AP=120); evaluable for efficacy: 232 CML-CP and 105 CML-AP.
pivotal_trials.result: CML-CP (n=232): major cytogenetic response 40% (95% CI 33, 46), complete 28% (22, 34). CML-AP (n=105): hematologic response 26% (95% CI 18, 35), complete hematologic response 18% (11, 27).

key_safety: Most common drug-related adverse reactions (>10%) in CML-CP: rash (33%), pruritus (29%), nausea (31%), headache (31%), fatigue (28%), diarrhea (22%), constipation (21%), vomiting (21%). Grade 3/4 lab abnormalities included thrombocytopenia (CML-CP 28%, CML-AP 37%) and neutropenia (CML-CP 28%, CML-AP 37%). Tasigna prolongs the QT interval and sudden deaths have been reported.
target_moa: Nilotinib is an inhibitor of the Bcr-Abl kinase; it binds to and stabilizes the inactive conformation of the kinase domain of the Abl protein and can overcome imatinib resistance from Bcr-Abl kinase mutations. It also inhibits PDGFR and c-Kit.

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: QT PROLONGATION AND SUDDEN DEATHS — Tasigna prolongs the QT interval and sudden deaths have been reported; it should not be used in patients with hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, or long QT syndrome.

rems.type: No formal REMS; an education-based RiskMAP was proposed and agreed upon to minimize risks of QTc prolongation, drug-drug interactions, and food effects.

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not taken to the Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (ODAC) because FDA determined it did not warrant ODAC review.
